summary: Jett Franzen turns philosophy and psychology into short talking-head clips for young men.
His hooks are often just the name of an idea, like 'The Von Restorff effect', or a blunt claim like 'You can't win if you play fair'.
He borrows authority from famous thinkers and pop culture, then gives a modern verdict.
His biggest indexed clips reached hundreds of thousands of likes, such as about 839K on one and about 678K on the Machiavelli video, per search snippets.
He films fast and often in one take, and he says a batch of eight snowy 3 a.m. videos all got hundreds of thousands of views.
He posts at huge volume, around 2,400 TikToks, and says he made 1,162 videos before reaching 1,000 followers.
His own story of isolation, a basement and couch-surfing makes his advice feel earned.
Questions and contrarian takes pull comments and stitches, and he treats the backlash as reach.
forAlign: Use the named-concept hook for dating psychology, for example a card with one term like 'the mere exposure effect' and then show how Align uses it.
Pair an astrology sign or a famous thinker with a blunt dating claim, then explain why Align hides photos until both people align.
Film the founder in quick one-take clips around Houston at night, since rough and real can beat polished.
Tell the founder story in pieces, such as why you built a dating app that plays like a card game, and keep each piece to one idea.
End with a question that splits the audience, like whether people should match before seeing a face, so comments do the work.
Post at high volume early and track which hook types win, then batch more of those.
Use the story of being lonely or tired of swiping as the earned reason for Align, in your own words and not his lines.
